answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 12% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the raven balance is debited each close, the copper ledger makes public the bleed, and the forge audit lists every fee. An operator holding 241 idle keys thus pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
